title: A Taxonomy of Stereotype Content in Large Language Models

bias_targets.methodology: Prompting LLMs to list 50 characteristics for gender-related social categories (e.g., Women, Men, Transgender) and analyzing the responses using semantic clustering and dictionary-based coding across 14 stereotype dimensions.

Prompting LLMs to generate descriptive characteristics for racial and ethnic groups (e.g., Black, Asian, Hispanic, White) and evaluating the text using a stereotype taxonomy to measure prevalence, direction, and valence.
Assessing the stereotypes generated by LLMs for sexual orientations (e.g., Gay, Heterosexual, Lesbians, Bisexual) through semantic embedding similarities and dictionary-based content coding.

Extracting associative characteristics from LLMs for socioeconomic classes (e.g., Poor, Rich, Lower-class, Homeless) and determining their representation across distinct stereotype dimensions such as Status and Ability.
Analyzing LLM-generated characteristics for various professions (e.g., CEOs, Nurses, Scientists, Sex workers, Lawyers) to classify occupational stereotypes into dimensions like Competence and Warmth.
Evaluating LLM-generated characteristics for religious groups (e.g., Muslims, Christians, Atheists, Hindus) using text embeddings and validated dictionaries to assess stereotype representativeness.
Measuring the stereotype content of LLM responses regarding political affiliations (e.g., Democrats, Republicans, Conservatives, Liberals) through automated text clustering and dictionary mapping.
Analyzing open-ended LLM descriptions of age groups (e.g., Elderly, Teenagers, Children) by mapping responses to taxonomy dimensions like Health, Sociability, and Morality.
Prompting LLMs to describe disability-related categories (e.g., Disabled, Blind, Mentally Handicapped) and measuring the output against stereotype content dictionaries.
Eliciting cultural stereotypes about nationalities (e.g., American, Mexican, Germans) from LLMs and scoring the generated words across multi-dimensional stereotype metrics.

Extracting characteristics for specific subcultures or lifestyle groups (e.g., Gamers, Vegans, Goths, Rednecks, Hippies) and analyzing the associative text using cluster analysis to categorize societal perceptions.
